D005-D018_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling… different for about two months now. Things that never bothered me before suddenly feel charged with meaning. I keep thinking that my designs—my landscapes—are more than just projects; I sometimes believe I’m channeling something bigger, like I’m part of a universal blueprint that only I can fully understand. It sounds strange, I know, but it feels real. I’ve even wondered if I’m meant to deliver some kind of message through my work, like I was chosen.

At night, I feel things crawling on my skin—ants, maybe, or threads pulling at my arms—but when I turn on the light, there’s nothing. I’ve checked the sheets, the windows, everywhere. My husband says he sees no one, no sign of anything, but I *feel* it.  

I’ve had a lot on my mind since… well, a few years back, something happened. I don’t like to talk about it, but it’s always there. Still, these thoughts and sensations don’t seem connected. They came out of nowhere, not triggered by memories or anything specific. I’m not jumpy or avoiding places. I just feel like I’m seeing a hidden layer of the world—one that no one else notices.
D005-D018_h001.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D018_h001.answer: D & C. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h002.question:
I’ve been seeing things—just little things at first, like shadows moving in the corner of my eye, or faces in the mirrors that weren’t mine. Lately, it’s gotten clearer. Last week, I saw a man standing at the end of the galley during a flight, in full uniform, but no one else reacted. He just disappeared. I keep thinking passengers are talking about me, even when they’re not looking my way. Sometimes I catch a word—“her,” “late,” “knew”—and it feels intentional, like a warning. 

It’s been about two months now. I can’t sleep without dreaming, and I wake up certain someone was in the room. 

I’ve had some rough stuff happen—I was on a flight a while back that had severe turbulence, went viral online. We were all shaken, but I didn’t fall apart—at least not then. I don’t re-experience *that* moment, not like a flashback. But I feel… watched. Like the world’s sending me messages through overhead screens, safety demos, even seat numbers. 

My husband says I'm distant. I don’t tell him about the visions. He’d think I’m losing it. I wonder if I am. But if this is trauma, why don’t I feel afraid when I see them? And if it’s in my head, why do they look so real?
D005-D018_h002.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D018_h002.answer: D & C. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h003.question:
I’ve been having a hard time these past couple of months—ever since I lost my job, actually. Things just haven’t felt real sometimes. I keep hearing my wife on the phone late at night, whispering, and I’m certain she’s talking to someone else. I don’t know who, but I *know* it’s happening. She denies it, of course, but I can hear things… voices in the background when she’s not even on a call. At first, I thought it was the neighbors, but now I hear them when I’m alone—low voices, like someone’s warning me, calling me names.

Sleep’s nearly impossible. I’ll lie there and hear footsteps outside the bedroom, or a door creak, but when I check, nothing’s there. I thought maybe it was all tied to that accident I had years back—the one where a coworker didn’t make it—but honestly, those memories don’t come back much. Not like *this*. This feels separate. I’m not reliving things, just… watching my life unravel while hearing things no one else does.

I love my wife. I know I sound paranoid, but to me, it’s real. I can’t shake the feeling she’s hiding something—something’s off.
D005-D018_h003.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D018_h003.answer: D & C. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h004.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about two months now—things just don’t feel real sometimes. There’s this smell, like something rotting, but no one else notices it. It’ll come out of nowhere, even when I’m outside working, hands in the soil, sun on my back. I know it doesn’t make sense, but I can’t shake the feeling that people are talking about me, even when they’re not. Like, last week I was trimming hedges at a house, and the homeowners were laughing through the window—I just *knew* it was about me, about my clothes, my job. Maybe it sounds crazy, but it feels real.

I’ve had some rough stuff happen, yeah—things I don’t like to go back to—but I don’t see images or hear voices from it. Not exactly. I don’t relive it, but I guess I’m jumpy. Always scanning. At night, I might hear a noise and freeze, heart going, like I’m back somewhere else. But the smells, the sense that people are sending me messages in code—that’s separate. Or is it? I don’t sleep well. Keep thinking the world’s got a hidden layer I’m seeing, but I can’t tell if it’s truth or my head breaking.
D005-D018_h004.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D018_h004.answer: D & C. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h005.question:
I’ve been feeling uneasy these past couple of months—something just isn’t right. There’s a man I see sometimes while sitting by the window, a kind-looking fellow I don’t actually know, but I just know he cares about me. He doesn’t visit, but I feel he’s watching out for me, sending me signs. My daughter says he’s no one, but she doesn’t understand the messages he sends.  

And then, at night, I feel things—like fingers brushing my arm or someone tugging the edge of the blanket. I wake up and there’s nothing there. It startles me, makes it hard to sleep. I lived through some difficult times years ago, back when my husband was still alive—some things I don’t like to talk about—but I wouldn’t say these feelings now are from that. They feel different.  

I don’t relive those old moments, not exactly, and I don’t feel jumpy or haunted by them. But I can’t explain why I feel watched, or why I’m so sure about that man’s feelings. My mind feels clouded at times, like pieces are drifting. I still manage on my own, go to the market, talk with neighbors, but there’s this quiet hum of something just off.
D005-D018_h005.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D018_h005.answer: D & C. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h006.question:
I’ve been struggling for about seven months now—maybe a bit more. Things just don’t feel real sometimes. I can’t enjoy the things I used to, not even closing a big deal, which used to get me fired up. Nothing clicks. My wife says I’ve changed.  

There are times I think people are watching me—cameras in my office, maybe the neighbors. I know it sounds off, but I can’t shake it. Sometimes I adjust my tie or walk a certain way, not because I need to, but because it feels… necessary, like if I don’t, something’s out of sync. My assistant mentioned I’ve been doing this little hand gesture, almost like pointing at nothing. I didn’t even realize I was doing it.  

I’ve had this weight on me since… well, something happened a few years back. I was held up at gunpoint during a property inspection—traumatizing, sure—but I thought I’d moved past it. I don’t see the guy’s face or anything like that. No nightmares I can pinpoint. But ever since that incident, and especially these last few months, I feel detached, like I’m going through motions.  

I’m not hearing voices or seeing things, but I just can’t trust my surroundings like I used to. I don’t know if it’s all connected or if I’m just falling apart on my own.
D005-D018_h006.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder
D005-D018_h006.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h007.question:
I’ve been feeling… off for about seven months now. It started subtly—like I could sense things others couldn’t. At first, I thought it was intuition, but then I became convinced I was meant for something huge—like I was chosen to capture the *most important* moments in people’s lives, not just weddings, but moments that would change history. Sometimes I feel like my photos can heal people, that they carry energy. I know that sounds strange.

I’ve caught myself rocking slightly when I’m alone, even during shoots—just a small back-and-forth, like my body needs to release something. And talking? It’s harder. I don’t know how to say what I mean anymore, so I just… stop. My husband says I’ll go quiet for long stretches, even at dinner.

There was a bad incident last year—something happened during a wedding abroad. I don’t like to talk about it. I wasn’t hurt physically, but since then, I’ve felt detached, like I’m watching my life through a lens. I don’t know if it’s connected. I just know I’m not the same.
D005-D018_h007.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder
D005-D018_h007.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h008.question:
I’ve been off for about seven months now—things just don’t feel real anymore. I used to love playing my violin, the way the music would carry me, but now even during rehearsals, it’s like I’m watching myself from far away. Nothing excites me, not even solos I practiced for years. I used to imagine composing a concerto that would change classical music—the conductor told me I was destined for greatness, and for a while, I believed that… still do, actually. I feel like I’m meant to reveal something huge through sound, something only I can hear clearly.  

Lately, I’ve caught myself swaying side to side when I’m alone, sometimes tapping my bow hand rhythmically against my leg, over and over, even when I’m not playing. I don’t plan it—it just happens.  

There was an accident last year—our tour bus crashed. I wasn't seriously hurt, but… I don’t know if that’s connected. Sometimes I see shadows move like strings in the air, but I can’t tell if it’s from the trauma or if my mind is showing me deeper truths now. I don’t sleep well, but I don’t dream—just silence, and then the swaying starts again.
D005-D018_h008.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder
D005-D018_h008.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h009.question:
I’ve been off for about seven months now—maybe longer, it’s hard to track. Some days, I just sit in the truck between jobs and can’t bring myself to move. My hands won’t listen, and the world feels like it’s behind glass. My wife says I’ll stare at the wall for hours, not answering her. When I do talk, it’s like the words get stuck—I’ve got things in my head, but they won’t come out right. 

But then there are other times—clear times—when I know things others don’t. I can’t explain it, but I feel chosen, like I’m meant for something big. Not famous or rich, but… important. Like I could heal people if I just figured out how. My wife thinks it’s stress, says I haven’t been the same since my brother died in that accident last year. I was there, you know. But I don’t dream about it. At least, not that I remember. I just feel… disconnected. Like I’m not fully here. Some of my coworkers think I’m slowing down, and yeah, I guess I am. But it’s not laziness. It’s like my mind’s split in two.
D005-D018_h009.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder
D005-D018_h009.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h010.question:
I’ve been struggling for about seven months now—things just feel off. Some days, I’m convinced the world is ending, like everything’s going to collapse into nothing. It sounds crazy, I know, but it feels real when I’m in it. I’ve stopped talking as much—at least that’s what my clients tell me. I used to be sharp on calls, always closing deals, but now I just don’t have much to say. My words feel heavy.

There are moments, though, when I laugh at nothing—silly things, like a bird flying past my window or the way a house key sounds when jiggled. It just strikes me as funny, and I can’t stop. It’s embarrassing later, especially when I catch my reflection and see how tired I look.

I lost my husband five years ago—it changed everything. Sometimes I wonder if that’s part of this, but I don’t relive moments or see him or anything like that. Not really. I just… space out sometimes. I can’t sleep, and I keep thinking the house is going to vanish, or the sky will crack. I don’t know what’s real anymore. I still go to work, barely, but I don’t feel like myself.
D005-D018_h010.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder
D005-D018_h010.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h011.question:
I’ve been off for about four months now—can’t quite put my finger on when it started, but things just feel… off. Lately, I catch myself thinking people are sending me messages through little things: a news anchor pausing too long, a siren from a block away—it feels like it’s meant for me, part of some pattern only I can see. I know how that sounds. I’m trained to stay level-headed, but I can’t shake the sense that the world’s speaking in codes.

Sometimes, I freeze up without realizing—just standing in the kitchen or at the rig, arms held out like I’m holding something heavy. My wife noticed; she said I was “posing,” but it doesn’t feel like that. It’s like my body’s responding to something I can’t name. 

We’ve had close calls on the job—everyone has. Recently we pulled a kid from a collapsed building… didn’t make it. But I don’t relive it, not like before with other calls. No nightmares, not really. Just this constant buzz, like I’m wired wrong. I’m not sleeping much. My wife says I seem distant. I just feel… watched, like the walls know.
D005-D018_h011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D005-D018_h011.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h012.question:
I’ve been feeling really off for about four months now. At first, I thought it was just stress—things at work got hectic, and I was dating someone who started pulling away. But then I started being sure she was seeing someone else, even though I’ve got no proof. I’d hear her say she was working late, and I’d swear she was lying—even if her car was parked outside her place. I check her phone when she’s asleep. I know it sounds messed up, but I can’t shake the feeling.

Sometimes, I catch myself repeating things people say—like after a client asks, “You good, man?” I’ll mutter it back without realizing. One of my coworkers noticed and asked if I was okay. It embarrassed me. I used to be sharp, in control—now I feel like I’m losing grip.

There are moments I can’t explain—like the other day, I heard my dad’s voice calling my name in the gym locker room. He died two years ago in that accident… but I didn’t *see* him or anything. Just the voice. I don’t know if it’s grief, or if something’s really wrong. I haven’t had nightmares or anything, really. Just this constant unease—like I’m being watched, even when I’m alone.
D005-D018_h012.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D005-D018_h012.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h013.question:
I’ve been feeling really off for about four months now—like my mind’s playing tricks on me. At work, I’ll be sanding a piece or fitting joints, and suddenly I get this overwhelming feeling that my ex is sneaking around with someone, even though we’ve barely spoken since the divorce two years ago. I don’t have proof, but the thought sticks, like I can *feel* it’s true. It makes me act silly sometimes—laughing at nothing, making goofy faces when I’m alone in the shop, things I’d never have done before. I know it sounds strange.  

There are moments—usually at night—when I can almost hear voices, like whispers behind a door, but when I turn, there’s nothing. And sometimes, for a split second, I think I see someone in the corner of the workshop, but it’s just a shadow. I don’t know if it’s related, but years ago I went through something bad—personal, hard to talk about—but that was long before these thoughts started. I don’t have nightmares about it, not really, and it doesn’t come back in flashes or anything. Still, I can’t shake this sense that things aren’t real sometimes. I just want to work, to keep my hands busy, but my head won’t let me.
D005-D018_h013.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D005-D018_h013.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h014.question:
Lately, it’s like I’m living inside one of my documentaries—except I’m not just filming it, I’m part of the story in a way I can’t explain. For about four months now, I’ve felt… chosen, like I’m meant to reveal truths no one else can see. I’ve been standing for hours in certain poses, almost like I’m channeling something—arms out, head tilted up—like I’m receiving signals. It sounds strange, I know, but I can *feel* the energy. I’m meant to deliver a message the world isn’t ready for.  

There are times when things shift—lights pulse in rhythm with my thoughts, or I hear whispers in the static of a paused microphone. Not full voices, just… implications. I used to think it was creative intuition, but now it feels deeper, like I’ve crossed into a hidden layer of reality.  

I don’t sleep much. When I close my eyes, I feel watched, and sometimes I see shadows that weren’t there before—brief, like a flicker on old film. I’ve had some rough experiences in war zones over the years, but I don’t think this is about that. Or maybe it is? I can’t tell anymore. I just know I’m not the same man I was.
D005-D018_h014.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D005-D018_h014.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h015.question:
I’ve been off since about four months ago—right around when my ex got remarried. I don’t know why it hit me so hard; our marriage was over for years. But ever since then, I can’t shake the feeling he’s been lying to me this whole time, that he never really let go and was pretending even while we were still together. I catch myself replaying old conversations, looking for clues. My coworkers have pointed out I sometimes repeat things they say, like a echo—I don’t even notice until it happens.

I work nights on the psych ward, so I’m used to intense situations, but lately I’ve been jumpy, like I’m waiting for something bad to happen. Sometimes I hear a name called out over the intercom, and it sounds like someone from years ago—someone connected to a bad incident I’d rather forget. But I can’t be sure it’s real. I tell myself it’s just fatigue, but it’s not just sleep. There’s a weight in my chest, like something’s buried but trying to surface. I don’t see things, not exactly, but there are moments when the past feels too close, like a whisper just behind me. I don’t know if it’s connected to him, or to what happened before, but I can’t untangle it.
D005-D018_h015.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D005-D018_h015.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h016.question:
I’ve been having a hard time since my wife passed… just over three months now. I work nights at the old warehouse—quiet, but the lights flicker sometimes, and I swear I feel something crawling under my skin, like bugs burrowing into my arms. I scratch, but there’s nothing there. The doctor said my liver’s fine, but I *know* something’s wrong inside—something’s rotting, I can feel it. 

I don’t talk much anymore. Hard to get the words out, and when I do, they don’t always come right—silly rhymes slip out, like “light” and “fight,” or “clock” and “shock.” I don’t mean to, it just happens. The silence gets heavy, though. I used to hum tunes—I was a trucker once, long hauls, you need the songs—but now even that feels off.

Sometimes I wake up soaked, heart pounding. I *think* I hear her voice, but it’s not her, not really. More like an echo. I don’t see her, not clearly. And I can’t say if it’s connected to the old fire I survived years back—been trying to forget that. I don’t dream about flames or anything. Just… emptiness. And the buzzing under my skin.
D005-D018_h016.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D018_h016.answer: D & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h017.question:
I’ve been off for about three months now—maybe longer, it’s hard to track. Things just feel… off. I keep tasting something metallic, like blood, but my husband checks my mouth and there’s nothing there. Food turns bitter no matter what I eat. Sometimes I think the lab team is spiking my water, not because they hate me, but because they’re feeding data to some larger system. I don’t know who’s collecting it. I’ve stopped going in—there are days I just don’t get out of bed. It’s not that I’m sad, exactly. It’s like the plan for the day—the whole structure—just dissolves before it starts.

I tried explaining it to my husband last week, but the words came out tangled. He said I was talking like a corrupted script, sentences looping, variables not resolving. I couldn’t fix it. I wanted to say, “I feel watched, not in a metaphorical way, but mathematically certain,” but instead I said something about enzymes breaking down signals, or maybe surveillance?

We had that break-in two years ago—does that matter? I wasn’t hurt. But sometimes I wonder if my system’s been compromised since then, like a dormant exploit. I don’t have nightmares. At least, not ones I remember.
D005-D018_h017.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D018_h017.answer: D & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h018.question:
I’ve been feeling… off for about three months now. Things people say on the street, even things on social media—they feel like they’re meant for me, coded messages. I’ll walk past someone laughing and I just *know* it’s about me, even if there’s no reason. Sometimes, I feel like someone’s brushing my arm, but when I look, there’s nothing. It’s happened while I’m sketching at my studio, the fabric shop—even at home. It’s not painful, but it makes my skin crawl.

I’ve stopped going to bridal expos. My assistant asked me last week if I’d call a client back, and I started talking about my favorite lace trim—completely lost track of why we were talking. I don’t mean to. It just happens. I used to love meeting brides, hearing their visions. Now I cancel appointments. I don’t want to be around anyone.

Something hard happened a while back, but I don’t think it’s connected—those feelings, the sensations, they didn’t start right after. They came later. Quietly. And I don’t relive it, not really. Just… this distance. Like I’m behind glass.
D005-D018_h018.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D018_h018.answer: D & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h019.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about three months now—maybe longer, but that’s when it started getting hard to ignore. At first, it was little things: I’d catch movement in the mirrors at the salon, figures standing in the corner who weren’t there when I turned. Now I see them more often—people in dark coats, just watching. I don’t know who they are, but I know they’re following me. They’re part of this network, I think… tracking what I do, syncing with my thoughts.  

Sometimes I’ll hear my name in the sound of the hairdryers—*hiss, hiss, miss, bliss*—and it feels like the words are linking up on their own, like they’re meant to. Makes sense in the moment.  

I used to love opening the shop, styling clients, but now I just… don’t. I cancel shifts. Sit at home. The motivation’s gone. I used to be good at reading people—part of the job—but now I feel like everyone’s part of it.  

There was a bad incident years back—something personal—but I don’t see how it connects. That was then. This feels separate. New. Different. I can’t sleep, but I don’t know if it’s from fear… or if they’re watching through the walls again.
D005-D018_h019.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D018_h019.answer: D & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h020.question:
I’ve been off since my wife passed—three months now, maybe more. The shop’s still running, but I don’t go in much anymore. Used to take pride in the cut, the rhythm of it, but now… I just stand there some days, knife in hand, like I forgot why I’m there. Doesn’t feel worth doing, most things.  

Lately, everything tastes like blood. Not the meat—*me*. Swallow water, eat bread, still metallic, like sucking on a battery. Doctor says test results are fine, but I *know* what I taste. And people talk when they think I can’t hear. At the diner, the waitress says “needs more salt” and I’m convinced she means *me*, like I’m spoiled, rotten. Saw a cop outside the shop last week, just standing. Didn’t do anything, just watched. I took it as a sign—knew they were onto me, somehow, about… I don’t know, something buried.  

Trying to explain it just comes out tangled. Words get stuck or spill over each other, and then I shut down. My brother says I’m not making sense, but I *feel* clear. Just… crowded.  

There was a bad time years back—can’t talk about it. But this? This isn’t that. At least, I don’t think it is.
D005-D018_h020.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D018_h020.answer: D & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h021.question:
I’ve been having these strange experiences for about three months now—long enough that I can’t just brush them aside. Sometimes, I catch a whiff of perfume, like roses, but no one’s around, and no flowers are nearby. It happens out of nowhere, even in class. I mentioned it once to a coworker, and she gave me this look, so I stopped talking about it.

There’s also this man—I don’t know him personally, but I’m certain he’s been sending me signals. He’s on the news sometimes, just a local businessman, but I feel this deep connection. He doesn’t have to say it; I just *know* he’s in love with me. I sometimes catch myself standing perfectly still, like posing for a photo, just holding that position without realizing how long it’s been. My students stare, and I snap out of it, embarrassed.

I’ve had some tough stuff in my past, things I don’t like to go over, but I don’t see how it’s connected. I’m not reliving it or anything—I just feel… watched. Not unsafe, exactly. More like everything has a hidden meaning now. I worry I’m losing my mind, but I show up to work, I sing songs with the kids, I’m not “crazy” in the way people think.
D005-D018_h021.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D018_h022.question:
Lately, it’s like my mind’s been playing these messed-up tricks on me. For about three months now, I keep hearing voices—low murmurs, like someone’s whispering behind a wall, but no one’s there. Sometimes they say the world’s already ended, that everything’s a lie and we’re just ghosts going through the motions. I know that sounds insane, but it feels real when I hear it.  

I’ve caught myself making these weird faces—frowning or twisting my mouth—without realizing it. My roommate mentioned it, which embarrassed me. I work long hours analyzing system vulnerabilities, staring at screens in the dark, and honestly, it’s been tough to stay grounded. There was… something that happened a while back, something bad, but I don’t want to talk about it right now. I don’t think it’s connected to the voices—those started way after.  

I’m not having nightmares or jumping at sounds or anything like that. But sometimes, out of nowhere, I get this chill, like something’s watching. I can’t shake the feeling that everything—technology, people, even time—is collapsing slowly, and I’m one of the few who sees it. I just don’t know what’s real anymore.
D005-D018_h022.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D018_h022.answer: C & B. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h023.question:
I’ve been working as a content moderator for about eight months now—watching videos people flag, most of them violent or disturbing. Lately, everything just feels… wrong. Like, the world isn’t real anymore. I keep thinking it’s all going to end—suddenly, completely—like there’s a rot underneath everything, even me. That thought won’t leave me alone.  

For the past three months, I’ll be sitting at my desk or lying in bed and suddenly taste something terrible—like metal or burning plastic—when I haven’t eaten anything. It makes me gag, but no one else tastes it. I can’t explain it.  

There are days when I just shut down. I don’t move. I don’t answer texts. I’ll stare at the wall for hours, not because I want to, but like I’m trapped inside my body. I don’t know if it’s because of the job—the things I’ve seen have definitely stuck with me—but the thoughts and the tastes? They don’t feel like memories. They feel like… something else.  

I don’t know if I’m breaking from reality or if I’m just stuck in it too hard. I haven’t been sleeping. I don’t talk much anymore. I just… wait.
D005-D018_h023.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D018_h023.answer: C & B. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h024.question:
I’ve been struggling for about three months now—maybe a little longer. Things feel… off. Like people at work are talking about me, even when they’re not looking at me. A teller once said "something’s rotten" under her breath, and I keep thinking she meant *me*, like I’m decaying or unclean. I’ve caught the smell—burnt hair or sewage—coming from nowhere, no source, but I know it’s there. I spray air freshener in my office, but it doesn’t help.

I pace a lot—my wife says I wear holes in the carpet. I can’t sit still, even when I’m exhausted. My mind races.  

A few years back, I was held at gunpoint during a bank robbery. I thought I'd moved past it, but lately, I wonder. Not that I relive it exactly—no vivid images or sudden jumps. It’s more like… a weight. I don’t dream about it. I just feel exposed, like I’m always being watched, even in safe places.  

But no, the smells and the sense that people are sending me messages through the news—they don’t feel connected to that event. It’s like it’s happening now, in real time. I don’t feel numb or avoidant. I just feel… tuned into a frequency no one else hears.
D005-D018_h024.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D018_h024.answer: C & B. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h025.question:
I’ve been struggling for about three months now—things just feel off, like my mind is playing tricks on me. At first, I thought it was stress. I work in a quiet corner of the city library, mostly alone with the shelves, so I have time to think… maybe too much time. Lately, I keep getting this bitter taste in my mouth, like copper or something spoiled, even when I haven’t eaten anything. It comes out of nowhere.

And then there’s Mark. We’ve been talking for a while—he’s a regular who comes in to read history books. I know it sounds strange, but I can’t shake the feeling he’s involved with someone else, even though he’s always polite, always the same. Nothing’s changed, but I *know*—I just *know*—he’s hiding something.

I catch myself doing odd little things, like organizing the same row of books over and over, tapping the spines in a certain order. It feels necessary, like if I don’t, something worse might happen. I don’t talk about it much. People already look at me funny.

Something from years ago sometimes creeps in—the memory of being followed home late one night, years back—but I don’t know if that’s connected. I don’t have nightmares or see images, not really. It’s just… a weight sometimes. Like the past is whispering, but I can’t make out the words.
D005-D018_h025.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D018_h025.answer: C & B. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
